claims.claim: MongoDB's Q2 FY2027 Form 10-Q provides current primary-source downside evidence that international exposure is material: 46% of revenue was generated outside the United States in each of FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024, creating exposure to regional political/economic conditions, currency effects and international operating complexity.

The same filing states technology-stock and MongoDB share-price volatility can be driven by operating-result variance, analyst expectations, competitive product announcements and investor perceptions of whether MongoDB is an AI beneficiary; this supports expectation-sensitivity as a source-addressed risk without asserting a numeric risk score.

MongoDB reported $2.4 billion of cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments at July 31, 2026, which is a resilience offset to the identified execution and market risks rather than evidence that those risks are absent.

causalEdges.mechanism: regional economic, political, currency and compliance conditions can alter demand and cost execution
investor perception and competitive announcements can amplify valuation volatility independently of realized workload economics
cash and short-term investments provide capacity to absorb operating volatility while product and consumption risks are tested

risks.risk: International exposure is structurally meaningful because 46% of revenue was generated outside the United States in each of the last three fiscal years cited by the filing.
Market expectations around AI beneficiary status and competitive announcements can amplify share-price volatility beyond underlying operating changes.

unknowns.unknown: The filing establishes exposure classes but does not by itself quantify the probability or earnings sensitivity of each downside; numeric underwriting remains Council Alpha-owned.
